q: The Indradhanush mission to revamp public sector banks was launched by which of the following?
explain: Indradhanush was launched in August 2015 by the then Finance Minister, Arun Jaitley.

q: In which year was the Indradhanush mission launched?
explain: The seven-point plan was launched in August 2015. Indradhanush 2.0 came later, in 2017.

q: How many elements does the Indradhanush plan to revamp PSBs have?
explain: Indradhanush has seven elements, like the seven colours of a rainbow: Appointments, BBB, Capitalisation, De-stressing, Empowerment, Framework of Accountability and Governance Reforms.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Indradhanush mission?
explain: Demonetisation (2016) is a separate measure. The seven prongs are A to G: Appointments, Banks Board Bureau, Capitalisation, De-stressing, Empowerment, Framework of Accountability, Governance Reforms.

q: The Banks Board Bureau, announced under Indradhanush, is best described as a(n)
explain: The Bureau is an autonomous, recommendatory body of eminent professionals and officials; it replaced the Appointments Board.

q: How many ex-officio members does the Banks Board Bureau have?
explain: The Bureau has 3 ex-officio members from the Government and 3 expert members, two of whom are from the private sector.

q: Under the Indradhanush roadmap, how much capital did the Government plan to infuse into state-run banks over four years?
explain: The Government planned ₹70,000 crore over four years, and the banks were to raise a further ₹1.1 lakh crore from the market to meet Basel III needs.

q: What is 'Gyan Sangam' in the context of public sector banks?
options: An annual general body meeting of shareholders
explain: Gyan Sangam was a conclave of PSBs and financial institutions, attended by the Prime Minister, Finance Minister, RBI Governor and bank CMDs.

q: In which city was the Gyan Sangam bankers' conclave held in early 2015?
explain: Gyan Sangam was organised in Pune at the start of 2015 and started the governance reform process.

q: Which bank received the highest amount of capital in the 2015-16 capitalisation of public sector banks?
explain: SBI received the largest allocation (about ₹5,531 crore), followed by Bank of India and IDBI Bank.

q: Under the Indradhanush roadmap, how much were PSBs expected to raise from the markets to meet capital needs?
explain: Besides the Government's ₹70,000 crore, banks had to raise a further ₹1.1 lakh crore from the markets, in line with Basel III.

q: How much capital were PSBs given in 2015-16 under the Indradhanush plan?
explain: PSBs were given ₹25,000 crore in 2015-16, the first year of the four-year plan.

q: Over how many years did the Government plan to infuse ₹70,000 crore into PSBs under Indradhanush?
explain: The ₹70,000 crore was to be infused over four years.

q: In which year did the Government announce Indradhanush 2.0?
explain: Indradhanush 2.0 came in 2017 as a comprehensive recapitalisation plan, in contrast to the original 2015 launch.

q: Indradhanush 2.0 was linked to the completion of which RBI exercise?
explain: The plan followed the Asset Quality Review (AQR) by the RBI and aimed at cleaning PSB balance sheets and revising capitalisation.

q: Indradhanush 2.0 aimed to help PSBs meet the capital adequacy norms of which framework?
explain: The plan was to recapitalise PSBs so that they remain solvent and comply with the global Basel III capital adequacy norms.

q: Which statement about the 'Appointments' element of Indradhanush is correct?
options: The Chairman and MD posts were separated, and private-sector candidates may apply for MD and CEO
The CMD post was abolished only for private banks
All PSB heads must now be IAS officers
The RBI Governor must chair every PSB board
explain: Separate posts of Chairman and MD/CEO were created in PSBs and private-sector executives can apply for the MD and CEO role.

q: Under the 'De-stressing' element of Indradhanush, which institutions were strengthened to deal with bad loans?
explain: De-stressing focused on relieving banks of NPAs, and asset reconstruction companies were strengthened to deal with the bad-loan situation.

q: Which measure did the Government consider under the 'Empowerment' element for PSB managements?
explain: Empowerment made hiring easier for PSBs and looked at ESOPs for their managements as incentives.

q: What does the 'Framework of Accountability' in Indradhanush introduce?
options: Mandatory RBI nominees on every board
Key performance indicators for state-run lenders
explain: A new framework of KPIs was announced to boost efficiency, while assuring banks independence in purely commercial decisions.

q: As a result of Gyan Sangam, each public sector bank agreed to nominate a senior officer as its
explain: Gyan Sangam recommendations included strengthening risk management; each bank agreed to nominate a Chief Risk Officer.

q: By which name is the Indradhanush plan for public sector banks also known?
explain: Its seven elements run alphabetically from A (Appointments) to G (Governance Reforms), hence the name A2G.

q: Which pair of Indradhanush elements and their features is correctly matched?
options: Framework of Accountability – key performance indicators
explain: KPIs belong to the Framework of Accountability. ARCs belong to de-stressing, ESOPs to empowerment and Gyan Sangam to governance reforms.

q: Which of the following banks was among the 13 PSBs capitalised under the 2015-16 Indradhanush allocation?
explain: The allocation went to public sector banks only, including Dena Bank. Axis, HDFC and ICICI are private sector banks.
